rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad was not present to witness these events; he learned them through God's revelation and instruction.
rows.anchor: ففي قوله عز وجل: {إذ يلقون أقلامهم} [آل عمران: 44] دلالة على محذوف من الكلام، وهو: «لينظروا أيهم يكفل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says they cast lots over Mary, an unseen event of which Muhammad knew only when God informed him.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {وما كنت لديهم إذ يلقون أقلامهم} [آل عمران: 44] قال: «حيث اقترعوا على مريم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cast lots to determine who had the strongest claim and was most entitled to care for Mary; the verse leaves that purpose implicit.
rows.anchor: ففي قوله عز وجل: {إذ يلقون أقلامهم} [آل عمران: 44] دلالة على محذوف من الكلام، وهو: «لينظروا أيهم يكفل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the implied sense might suggest an accusative, أي is the subject of an interrogative inquiry after verbs of looking, discerning, and knowing.
rows.anchor: فقد ظن خطأ؛ وذلك أن النظر والتبين والعلم مع «أي» يقتضي استفهاما واستخبارا، وحظ «أي» في الاستخبار الابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كفل means to take in or care for; al-Tabari says he established this meaning earlier.
rows.anchor: وقد دللنا فيما مضى قبل أن معنى يكفل يضم، بما أغنى عن إعادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad was absent when Mary's people disputed which of them was most entitled to care for her.
rows.anchor: يعني بذلك جل ثناؤه: وما كنت يا محمد عند قوم مريم، إذ يختصمون فيها أيهم أحق بها وأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This address rebukes disbelieving Jews and Christians: Muhammad reports events he did not witness, without reading their books or learning from their scholars.
rows.anchor: فتوبيخ منه عز وجل للمكذبين به من أهل الكتابين، يقول: كيف يشك أهل الكفر بك منهم،

rows.speaker: محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq transmits from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr that the revelation disclosed concealed knowledge about their dispute, confirming Muhammad's prophethood and establishing proof against them.
rows.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، عن محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير: {وما كنت لديهم إذ يختصمون} [آل عمران: 44] «أي ما كنت معهم إذ يختصمون فيها

rows.speaker: قراء الحجاز من مكة والمدينة وقراء الكوفة
rows.claim: The majority of readers in the Hijaz and Kufa read both verbs as direct address: تبغون and ترجعون.
rows.anchor: وأولى ذلك بالصواب قراءة من قرأ: (أفغير دين الله تبغون) على وجه الخطاب (وإليه ترجعون) بالتاء، لأن الآية التي قبلها خطاب لهم،

rows.speaker: بعض أهل الحجاز
rows.claim: Some Hijazi readers use third person for both verbs: يبغون and يرجعون.
rows.anchor: بعض أهل الحجاز: {أفغير دين الله يبغون}

rows.speaker: بعض أهل البصرة
rows.claim: Some Basran readers use third person in يبغون, then address the audience in ترجعون.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ذلك بعض أهل البصرة: {أفغير دين الله يبغون} [آل عمران: 83] على وجه الخبر عن الغائب، «وإليه ترجعون» بالتاء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari prefers direct address in both verbs because the preceding verse addresses the same audience; switching between address and third person is nevertheless permissible in reported speech.
rows.anchor: وأولى ذلك بالصواب قراءة من قرأ: (أفغير دين الله تبغون) على وجه الخطاب (وإليه ترجعون) بالتاء، لأن الآية التي قبلها خطاب لهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here God's religion means obedience to God.
rows.anchor: تأويل الكلام: يا معشر أهل الكتاب: (أفغير دين الله تبغون) يقول: أفغير طاعة الله تلتمسون وتريدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All in the heavens and earth humble themselves before God, serve him, affirm his exclusive lordship, and yield to his sole divinity.
rows.anchor: يقول: وله خشع من في السموات والأرض، فخضع له بالعبودية وأقر له بإفراد الربوبية،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels, prophets, and messengers submit willingly; the phrase also encompasses those whose submission is reluctant.
rows.anchor: وذلك كالملائكة والأنبياء والمرسلين، فإنهم أسلموا لله طائعين، وكرها من كان منهم كارها.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains reluctant submission as acknowledging God as creator and lord even while associating other beings with him in worship, likening it to the admission in 29:61.
rows.anchor: عن سفيان، عن منصور، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya says every person has acknowledged God as lord and himself as God's servant; the polytheist submits reluctantly, while the sincere servant does so willingly.
rows.anchor: عن الربيع، عن أبي العالية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas, transmitted by Mujahid, says submission by compulsion refers to the primordial covenant.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، عن ابن عباس: {وله أسلم من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها} قال: «حين أخذ الميثاق»

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the unbeliever's shadow as submitting unwillingly; in another report he describes the believer's prostration as willing and the unbeliever's as reluctant, including the unbeliever's shadow.
rows.anchor: الطائع: المؤمن، وكرها: ظل الكافر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: A further Mujahid report says both a person's face and shadow prostrate willingly.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن كثير، عن مجاهد، قال: «سجود وجهه وظله طائعا»

rows.speaker: عامر
rows.claim: Amir says that all submit to God and yield to his command, even if they verbally deny his divinity.
rows.anchor: عن عامر: {وله أسلم من في السموات والأرض} قال: «استقاد كلهم له»

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says some people were compelled to embrace Islam while others came willingly.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {وله أسلم من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها} الآية كلها، فقال: «أكره أقوام على الإسلام، وجاء أقوام طائعين»

rows.speaker: مطر الوراق
rows.claim: Matar al-Warraq says angels, the Ansar, Banu Sulaym, and Abd al-Qays submitted willingly, while all other people submitted reluctantly.
rows.anchor: عن مطر الوراق، في قول الله عز وجل: {وله أسلم من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها وإليه يرجعون} قال: «الملائكة طوعا، والأنصار طوعا،

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another view says believers submit willingly, while unbelievers submit reluctantly only when facing death, when their submission no longer benefits them.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: معنى ذلك أن أهل الإيمان أسلموا طوعا، وأن الكافر أسلم في حال المعاينة حين لا ينفعه إسلام كرها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says believers submit willingly and benefit from accepted faith, whereas unbelievers submit only when they see God's punishment, too late for it to benefit or be accepted; he cites 40:85.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {وله أسلم من في السموات والأرض طوعا وكرها} قال: «أما المؤمن فأسلم طائعا، وأما الكافر فأسلم حين رأى بأس الله»

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the willing and reluctant submission as all creation's worship of God, linking it to the prostration of all in the heavens and earth in 22:18.
rows.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jews, Christians, and all others return to God after death for recompense according to their deeds; this warns them not to die outside Islam.
rows.anchor: وإليه يا معشر من يبتغي غير الإسلام دينا من اليهود والنصارى، وسائر الناس (ترجعون) يقول: إليه تصيرون بعد مماتكم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes matters easier by permitting a man unable to afford a free woman to marry a believing bondwoman when he fears sexual sin.
rows.anchor: يريد الله أن يخفف عنكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings are weak because they have little patience for abstaining from intercourse; the permission prevents fornication when they cannot afford a free woman.
rows.anchor: لأنكم خلقتم ضعفاء عجزة عن ترك جماع النساء قليلي الصبر عنه، فأذن لكم في نكاح فتياتكم المؤمنات،

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the easing concerns marriage to a bondwoman and, more generally, everything in which God grants ease.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد: {يريد الله أن يخفف، عنكم} [النساء: 28] في نكاح الأمة، وفي كل شيء فيه يسر

rows.speaker: طاوس
rows.claim: Tawus interprets human weakness specifically in matters of intercourse and women.
rows.anchor: عن ابن طاوس، عن أبيه: {وخلق الإنسان ضعيفا} [النساء: 28] قال: «في أمر الجماع»

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says God permitted marriage to bondwomen in cases of need; without this concession, a man unable to find a free woman would remain under the original ruling.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {يريد الله أن يخفف عنكم} [النساء: 28] قال: " رخص لكم في نكاح هؤلاء الإماء حين اضطروا إليهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's favor and guidance protected Muhammad and clarified the traitor's case, so Muhammad refrained from arguing for him or defending him against the rightful claimant.
rows.anchor: الله تفضل عليك يا محمد فعصمك بتوفيقه وتبيانه لك أمر هذا الخائن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faction tried to lead Muhammad from the right judgment by disguising the traitor's case, testifying that he was innocent, and asking Muhammad to excuse and defend him among his companions.
rows.anchor: وذلك لتلبيسهم أمر الخائن عليه صلى الله عليه وسلم وشهادتهم للخائن عنده بأنه بريء مما ادعي عليه، ومسألتهم إياه أن يعذره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They misled themselves by taking a forbidden path and aiding the wrongdoer rather than the people he had wronged; God's command was to avoid aiding sin and to help what is right. The earlier prohibition on defending traitors is 4:105.
rows.anchor: في كتابه على لسان رسوله إلى خلقه بالنهي عن أن يتعاونوا على الإثم والعدوان والأمر بالتعاون على الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their attempt cannot harm Muhammad: God will strengthen and guide him, reveal their effort to mislead him, and expose both the plotters and the traitor.
rows.anchor: لأن الله مثبتك ومسددك في أمورك ومبين لك أمر من سعوا في ضلالك عن الحق في أمره وأمرهم، ففاضحه وإياهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book is the Qur'an, containing clarification of everything, guidance, and admonition.
rows.anchor: وهو القرآن الذي فيه بيان كل شيء، وهدى وموعظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom is what the Book states in summary: its lawful and forbidden matters, commands and prohibitions, rulings, promises, and warnings.
rows.anchor: هي ما كان في الكتاب مجملا ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God taught Muhammad accounts of earlier and later peoples and what had happened or would happen; this too is God's favor.
rows.anchor: وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God has shown Muhammad immense favor, he should thank God through obedience, hasten to God's pleasure, keep to revelation, and oppose those trying to divert him; God will protect him, while no one can save him if he disobeys and follows their desire.
rows.anchor: فإن الله هو الذي يتولاك بفضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse alerts Muhammad to his own welfare and reminds him of the duty he owes God.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية تنبيه من الله نبيه محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم على موضع حظه، وتذكير منه له الواجب عليه من حقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is to recount the story to Jews who planned violence against him and his companions, warning them through the outcomes of injustice, treachery, and broken covenants: the faithful son was rewarded and the oathbreaker punished.
rows.anchor: واتل على هؤلاء اليهود الذين هموا أن يبسطوا أيديهم إليكم، عليك وعلى أصحابك معك، وعرفهم مكروه عاقبة الظلم والمكر،

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One view says God commanded Adam's sons to offer sacrifices; the accepted offering came from the son who gave the best of his property, while the other gave its worst. They were Habil and Qabil, Adam's sons.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم: كان ذلك عن أمر الله جل وعز إياهما بتقريبه. وكان سبب القبول أن المتقبل منه قرب خير ماله

rows.speaker: إسماعيل بن رافع
rows.claim: Ismail ibn Rafi reports that the shepherd offered a beloved lamb, which God accepted; it continued grazing in Paradise until it was offered as ransom for Abraham's son.
rows.anchor: عن هشام بن سعيد، عن إسماعيل بن رافع، قال: بلغني أن ابني آدم لما أمرا بالقربان، كان أحدهما صاحب غنم،

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr says the shepherd offered his fattest, best sheep willingly, while the farmer grudgingly offered poor grain; God accepted the sheep, and the murdered brother was stronger but piety kept him from striking his brother.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو، قال: إن ابني آدم اللذين قربا قربانا

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: A contrary view says the sacrifice was not offered at God's command to the two brothers.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: لم يكن ذلك من أمرهما عن أمر الله إياهما به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says offerings were made because there were no poor people to receive charity; God accepted an offering by sending fire to consume it, while rejected offerings were left untouched. A shepherd offered his best sheep, a farmer his least-liked grain, and the rejected son threatened his brother out of shame; his brother answered that God accepts only from the pious.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه، عن ابن عباس، قال: كان من شأنهما أنه لم يكن مسكين فيتصدق عليه،

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the brothers as Adam's biological sons Habil and Qabil: one offered a sheep and the other vegetables or crops; the fire accepted the sheep, and the rejected brother killed its owner.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: A report heard from Mujahid says God bound one of Cain's legs to his thigh for life, turned his face toward the sun, and placed him under alternating winter shelters of ice and summer shelters of fire, attended by seven angels in succession.
rows.anchor: قال: ثنا رجل، سمع مجاهدا، في قوله: {واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم بالحق إذ قربا قربانا}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that one brother offered a ram and the other a heap of food; God accepted the offering of the sheep's owner. Another report from him simply identifies them as two Adamites, one accepted and one rejected.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، عن ابن عباس: {واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم بالحق إذ قربا قربانا فتقبل من أحدهما ولم يتقبل من الآخر} [المائدة: 27] قال: " قرب هذا كبشا وقرب هذا صبرة من طعام؛

rows.speaker: عطية
rows.claim: Atiyya says Qabil was a farmer and Habil a shepherd; one offered a choice lamb and the other inferior crops, so the fire consumed the lamb and Qabil threatened his brother.
rows.anchor: عن فضيل بن مرزوق، عن عطية: {واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم بالحق} [المائدة: 27] قال: " كان أحدهما اسمه قابيل والآخر هابيل؛

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق عن بعض أهل العلم بالكتاب الأول
rows.claim: A report from earlier-scripture scholars says Adam arranged cross-marriages between the twins; Habil accepted, but Qabil refused, claiming superiority and wanting his own twin sister. Some said Qabil's twin was especially beautiful and he coveted her. Adam settled the dispute by offering whichever son had his sacrifice accepted the right to marry the girl; Habil brought a prime lamb and Qabil grain (some say a cow), and a white fire consumed Habil's offering alone.
rows.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، عن بعض أهل العلم بالكتاب الأول: " أن آدم أمر ابنه قابيل أن ينكح أخته توأمة هابيل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari leaves uncertain which of the reported explanations for the brothers' marriage dispute was true.
rows.anchor: فالله أعلم أي ذلك كان.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi reports, through Abu Malik and Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas, Murrah from Ibn Masud, and other Companions, that each birth brought paired twins; Habil wanted Qabil's prettier twin, but Qabil refused. Adam left for Mecca after asking the heavens, earth, and mountains to guard the family; only Qabil agreed. Habil offered a fat young ewe while Qabil gave a bundle of grain after eating its best seed, and fire accepted Habil's offering, prompting Qabil's threat.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، فيما ذكر عن أبي مالك، وعن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس، وعن مرة، عن ابن مسعود، وعن ناس، من أصحاب النبي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Habil offered the best of his flock and fire consumed it, while Qabil offered inferior crops and the fire did not descend; accepted offerings were consumed by fire, but rejected ones were eaten by birds and beasts, leading Qabil to envy and threaten his brother.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم بالحق} [المائدة: 27] ذكر لنا أنهما هابيل وقابيل.
